solutions.17: ∠ABC = ½ × 130° = 65° (angle at the centre is double the angle on the circle). ∠ADC = 180° − 65° = 115° (ABCD is cyclic).
solutions.22: Let AB = CD be chords of a circle with centre O. In ΔAOB and ΔCOD: OA = OC, OB = OD (radii) and AB = CD. So ΔAOB ≅ ΔCOD (SSS), and ∠AOB = ∠COD (CPCT).
solutions.23: (a) OC = OD = CD, so ΔOCD is equilateral and ∠COD = 60°. (b) ∠CBD = ½ ∠COD = 30°. (c) ∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so ∠BCP = 90°. In ΔBCP, ∠APB = 180° − 90° − 30° = 60°.
solutions.24: (a) ∠BCD = 180° − 85° = 95° (cyclic quadrilateral). (b) ∠ABD = 180° − 85° − 40° = 55°. (c) ∠ACB = ∠ADB = 40°, because they are angles in the same segment on chord AB.

papers.caseStudy: A circular garden has centre O and radius 7 m. A gate G is 25 m from O. Two straight paths GA and GB touch the garden at A and B.

solutions.17: PA × PB = PC × PD, so 6 × 4 = PC × 3 and PC = 8 cm. CD = 8 + 3 = 11 cm.
solutions.18: PB = 4 + 5 = 9 cm. PT² = PA × PB = 36, so PT = 6 cm.
solutions.21: PA × PB = PC × PD. PB = 12, so 3 × 12 = 4 × PD and PD = 9. CD = 9 − 4 = 5 cm.
solutions.22: Let AB be a diameter, with tangents l at A and m at B. The radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so ∠(OA, l) = 90° and ∠(OB, m) = 90°. These are alternate angles on line AB, so l ∥ m.
solutions.24: (a) ∠OAG = 90°, so GA = √(25² − 7²) = √576 = 24 m. (b) GA = GB, because tangents from an external point are equal. (c) Area = 2 × ½ × 7 × 24 = 168 m².

solutions.18: Steps: join OP and bisect it at M. Draw a circle with centre M and radius MO. It cuts the given circle at T. Join PT. PT = √(6² − 2.5²) = √29.75 ≈ 5.45 cm, so the measure is about 5.5 cm.
solutions.19: Steps: draw a circle of radius 3 cm. Step off chords of 3 cm six times around it, and join the points. The radius of the circumcircle equals the side, 3 cm.
solutions.20: Steps: construct the triangle, bisect ∠B and ∠C, and mark the incentre I. Draw IM ⟂ BC and the circle with radius IM. AC² = 25 + 36 − 30 = 31, area ≈ 12.99 cm², s ≈ 8.28 cm, so r ≈ 1.6 cm.
solutions.21: Steps: construct the triangle and draw the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC. They meet at the mid-point of AC. AC = √(36 + 64) = 10 cm, so the radius is 5 cm.
solutions.22: The tangent from a point on the larger circle touches the smaller circle at T, with OT ⟂ PT. PT = √(4² − 2²) = √12 ≈ 3.46 cm, so the measure is about 3.5 cm.
solutions.23: (a) Bisect OP at M, draw the circle with centre M and radius MO, and join P to the two points A and B where it cuts the given circle. (b) PA = √(49 − 9) = √40 ≈ 6.3 cm. (c) sin(∠APO) = 3/7, so ∠APO ≈ 25.4° and ∠APB ≈ 51°.

notes.subtitle: Standard Loci, Circumcentre & Incentre

concepts.title: Locus
concepts.text: A locus is the set of all points that satisfy a given condition.

concepts.title: Standard loci
concepts.text: Fixed distance from a point: a circle. Equidistant from two points: the perpendicular bisector. Fixed distance from a line: two parallel lines.

concepts.title: Angle bisector
concepts.text: Points equidistant from two intersecting lines lie on the bisectors of the angles between them.

concepts.title: Triangle centres
concepts.text: The perpendicular bisectors meet at the circumcentre (equidistant from the vertices). The angle bisectors meet at the incentre (equidistant from the sides).

formulas: Equidistant from A and B → perpendicular bisector of AB
Equidistant from two lines → angle bisector
Fixed distance r from O → circle (O, r)
Circumradius R = abc/(4Δ); inradius r = Δ/s
method: Read each condition and name its locus.
Construct each locus with compasses.
Mark the intersection points of the loci.
Measure and state the answer with units.

example.question: Find the points that are 4 cm from A and equidistant from A and B, where AB = 6 cm.
steps: They meet at two points, √(16 − 9) = √7 ≈ 2.6 cm from AB.
example.answer: Two points, each about 2.6 cm from AB

notes.subtitle: Angle Properties & Cyclic Quadrilaterals

concepts.title: Angle at the centre
concepts.text: The angle that an arc subtends at the centre is double the angle that it subtends at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

concepts.title: Same segment
concepts.text: Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.

concepts.title: Semicircle
concepts.text: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle.

concepts.title: Cyclic quadrilateral
concepts.text: Opposite angles add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.

formulas: Angles in the same segment are equal
method: Mark the centre, the chords and the given angles on a rough figure.
Name the arc or chord that each angle stands on.
Use one property at a time and write its reason.
Use the angle sum of a triangle to finish.

notes.subtitle: Tangent Properties & Chord Products

concepts.title: Tangent and radius
concepts.text: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

concepts.title: Tangents from a point
concepts.text: The two tangents from an external point are equal, and they make equal angles with the line to the centre.

concepts.title: Alternate segment theorem
concepts.text: The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.

concepts.title: Intersecting chords and secants
concepts.text: PA × PB = PC × PD for chords (inside or outside). For a tangent PT and a secant PAB, PT² = PA × PB.

method: Mark the right angles between radii and tangents.
Look for equal tangents and isosceles triangles.
Use the alternate segment theorem for a tangent–chord angle.
Use the product rule for lengths of chords and secants.

notes.subtitle: Tangents, Circumcircles, Incircles & Hexagons

concepts.title: Tangent at a point
concepts.text: Draw the radius OP and construct a perpendicular to it at P.

concepts.title: Tangents from an external point
concepts.text: Bisect OP at M and draw a circle on OP as diameter. It cuts the given circle at the points of contact (angle in a semicircle = 90°).

concepts.title: Circumcircle and incircle
concepts.text: The circumcircle uses perpendicular bisectors of the sides. The incircle uses angle bisectors; its radius is the perpendicular from the incentre to a side.

concepts.title: Regular hexagon
concepts.text: The side of a regular hexagon equals the radius of its circumcircle.

formulas: Circumradius of a right triangle = hypotenuse/2
Equilateral triangle: R = a/√3, r = a/(2√3)
method: Draw a rough sketch with the given measures.
Construct the figure accurately with ruler and compasses.
Keep all arcs and label every point.

notes.subtitle: Surface Area, Volume & Recasting

concepts.title: Cylinder
concepts.text: CSA = 2πrh, TSA = 2πr(r + h), volume = πr²h.

concepts.title: Cone
concepts.text: l = √(r² + h²), CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(l + r), volume = ⅓πr²h.

concepts.title: Sphere and hemisphere
concepts.text: Sphere: SA = 4πr², volume = (4/3)πr³. Solid hemisphere: TSA = 3πr², volume = (2/3)πr³.

concepts.title: Recasting
concepts.text: When a solid is melted and recast, the volume stays the same.

method: Draw the solid and label r, h and l.
Choose the correct formula for each part.
For combined solids, add volumes; for surface area, add only exposed surfaces.
For recasting, set volume before = volume after.
